title: Breadator flour model: flour types, hydration method, scalds, vital gluten
status: sourced defaults for calculators; every default is replaceable by the mill's specification or by the baker's own calibrated recipe

units.percent: baker's % (total flour = 100) unless a basis is given
units.fibre: total dietary fibre, g/100 g as is
units.water_absorption: farinograph-equivalent absorption, % of flour at 14 % moisture, 500 BU, no salt
units.bread_hydration: total water in the bread dough incl. preferments and scalds, % of total flour

value_convention: Every value object carries `source` (claim ids of claims-*.jsonl, or bibliography keys) and `evidence`. When a measured point is widened into a range by reasoning, `evidence` labels the typical value and `range_evidence` the range; every extrapolation states its `reasoning`. Claim ids of other sources (novita-*, breadcode-*) are claims in the merged corpus.

flours.use: Pick the type; use `typical` as default and `range` as the 80 % band shown to the user. Ash is the legal or trade definition of the type; protein, fibre and absorption describe typical commercial flours of that type and must be replaced by the bag or mill specification when known. Absorption is for comparing flours and computing changes (hydration_method); bread_hydration is the usual total water of breads made mainly from that flour.

absorption_default.applies_to: Triticum aestivum flours (FR, DE, IT, US types) without a mill value
absorption_default.reasoning: intercept from a measured white type-530 flour (60.6 %) and an unsalted flour (62.8 %); ash slope reproduces T55 to T150 recipe water (+8) and refined to wholemeal farinograph gaps (+5.5 to +8); protein slope from Tipples 1978. Underestimates hard red spring flours with high starch damage by up to 6 points (66.0 % measured at 12.7 % protein, science-flour-0035).

hydration_method.use: Estimate the total dough water for a flour blend plus additions, with an uncertainty band. Two modes: A (no reference recipe) starts from the flour types' usual bread hydration; B (the baker has a recipe that works) carries the recipe's hydration over and adds only the absorption difference of the new flours. Both then add the water of fibres, seeds, vital gluten and scalds. Total water always includes the water of preferments, soakers and scalds; it is allocated to those stages, not added on top.

inputs.flours: list of {type id, mass f_i in g as is, optional protein P_i % as is, optional moisture M_i %, optional mill absorption A_i % at 14 % moisture}
inputs.additions: list of {kind, mass a_j in g}
inputs.scald: optional {share s of total flour, ratio r water per flour, method}

steps.name: flour absorption
steps.formula: A_i = mill value if known, else flours[type].water_absorption_pct.typical + 1.0 * (P_i - P_type) when the bag protein P_i is known
steps.note: +1.03 points per protein point at constant starch damage (Tipples 1978, r2 0.993 on 20 mill streams); valid within about 3 protein points of the type value

steps.name: moisture correction
steps.applies: when the flour moisture M_i is known and differs from 14 %
steps.reasoning: constant water per dry matter (the basis of the 14 % moisture convention); slope -1.86 points per moisture point at A = 60, against the empirical -1.97 of the Farrand equation

steps.name: blend
steps.formula: A_blend = sum(f_i * A_i) / F and H_flours = sum(f_i * H_i) / F with F = sum(f_i), H_i = flours[type].bread_hydration_pct.typical
steps.uncertainty: u_flours = sum(f_i * u_i) / F with u_i = half-width of the type's range (ranges move together, so they are added linearly), plus 2.5 points for wheat-rye blends with 10-40 % rye
steps.reasoning: an industry blend table departs from the linear mean by -0.8 to +2.4 points; a wholemeal study assumed additivity to back-calculate absorption

steps.name: base hydration, mode B
steps.uncertainty: u_B = sqrt(sum over flour types of (d_i * u_A,i)^2), d_i = change in the mass fraction of type i between the reference and the new blend, u_A,i = half-width of its absorption range (0.5 point for mill values); flours common to both blends cancel
steps.reasoning: a working recipe already encodes process, style and the baker's preferred consistency; only the flour difference is transferred. The same T65 takes 62 % in a straight dough and 68 % in a long tradition dough, so absolute style offsets are not portable

steps.name: additions
steps.formula: W_add = sum(a_j * k_j) g; H = H_base + 100 * W_add / F
steps.uncertainty: u_add_j = a_j * (k_max - k_min) / 2, combined in quadrature with u_flours * F / 100
steps.reasoning: coefficients below; each is measured at equal dough consistency where possible, else a soaker ratio

steps.name: scald
steps.formula: H = H + scalds.water_shift k * s_pct (s_pct = scalded flour % of total flour); allocate W_s = r * s * F to the scald

steps.name: salt (only when comparing with unsalted farinograph values)
steps.formula: dA = -3.1 * s_salt for s_salt <= 1; dA = -3.1 - 0.8 * (s_salt - 1) for 1 < s_salt <= 2 (salt % of flour)
steps.note: single flour; bread_hydration values already include normal salt, so mode A and mode B do not apply this step

steps.name: allocate water
steps.formula: W_total = H * F / 100; W_dough = W_total - W_scald - W_soakers - W_preferments; reject W_dough < 0
steps.reasoning: mass balance; counts every water once

addition_coefficients.note: +1.5 absorption points per 1 % gluten; gluten binds 1.35-2.15 g/g by component tables

addition_coefficients.reasoning: refined vs wholemeal farinograph absorption of one mill (65.98 vs 73.99 %, 68.93 vs 74.45 %) assigns 1.01-1.13 g/g to the 17 % bran and germ fraction; a cold soaker saturates bran at 2 g/g

addition_coefficients.note: pre-hydrate 2 h to saturation (1.6 g/g); more gives free water
9.55 g/g at equal consistency in wholegrain wheat dough (one study, 5 % dose); swelling 15 mL/g; soaker saturation 20-40 g/g. Gluten-free studies added up to 10 % without extra water: disagreement
5.55 g/g at equal consistency (one study); 5 % chia flour did not change farinograph absorption in another, 15 % raised it
5 % whole seeds slightly lowered farinograph absorption; seeds hydrate later, during fermentation
mucilage (about 6 % of the seed) binds 16-30 g/g
cold soaker; IREKS soaked grain TA 160-250
0.5-2 points of water per 1 % AX added

addition_coefficients.reasoning: β-glucan is the fibre that best explains extra flour absorption, but no per-gram coefficient was found; add water by feel or use oat bran

guards: W_dough < 0: the soakers and scald hold more water than the dough; lower their ratios or the scald share
additions above 15 % of flour (seeds, bran) or psyllium above 5 %: outside the tested range of the coefficients
absorption computed for a 500 BU farinograph dough: high-fibre doughs bake best softer (366 BU with pre-saturated oat bran), so treat H as a starting point and record the outcome

worked_example_B.recipe: a T65 recipe that works at 68 %; switch to 70 % T65 + 30 % T150 at 14 % moisture

component_water_binding.note: for explanation only, not for prediction: published coefficients disagree by up to 2x

scalds.use: Plan a scald (tangzhong, yudane, empois, Brühstück, Kochstück, rye scald): its flour and water stay part of the recipe totals; the model gives the share of flour, the water allocation, the extra dough water at equal consistency, whether the starch gelatinizes at the temperature reached, and the expected effects.

definitions.name: tangzhong (water roux, 1:5 style)
definitions.process: slurry heated while stirring until it thickens; cooled; used at once or chilled

definitions.name: Brühstück (boiling-water scald of meal, flakes or old bread)

wheat_starch_excess_water.note: the 76-86 % figure is an extrapolation combining two studies (science-flour-0081)

rule_complete.reasoning: wheat starch: onset 60.7 deg C in water, no enthalpy left after 71.0-73.6 deg C

water_dependence.excess_water: water at or above about 66-67 % of water + starch (water:starch about 2 or more): one endotherm, onset about 60-61 deg C for wheat. Flour is about 70 % starch, so a 1:2 or wetter scald is in this regime, while a 1:1 yudane (about 62 % water counting the flour's own moisture) sits just below it and gelatinizes less completely at the same temperature
water_dependence.limited_water: below about 66 % water a second, higher melting endotherm appears and spreads over 40-50 deg C; at 25 % water the peak rose to 74 deg C against 62 deg C at 35 %
water_dependence.renzetti_form: 1/Tm - 1/Tm0 = (R/dHu)(vu/vw)(phi_w - chi * phi_w^2), wheat Tm0 = 473 K (not implemented: molar volume ratio not available)
water_dependence.note: the regime assignment of 1:1 and 1:2 scalds is an extrapolation from these thresholds

other_starches.note: method-dependent; quoted textbook ranges (wheat 51-60, rice 68-78 deg C) sit lower or wider (science-flour-0085)

sugar_shift.variable: c = sugar / (sugar + water) * 100 in the water phase of the scald or dough

salt_shift.rule: per % NaCl on flour up to 2 %: onset about +0.8 deg C, peak +1.0, end +2.6 (non-linear: most of the onset shift comes from the first 1 %)
salt_shift.note: single dough study; a scald without salt is unaffected

water_shift.formula: dH (points of total hydration) = k * s_pct, with s_pct = scalded flour as % of total flour

k_by_method.method: 1:1 boiling-water yudane (mix ends near 55 deg C, starch partly gelatinized)
k_by_method.note: Yamauchi 68 -> 71 -> 74 % at 0/20/40 %; Tsuboi kept total water at 68 % for 10 and 20 %

k_by_method.method: hot scald held at 60-70 deg C (hot-soaked grain, Brühstück of flour)
paste cooked to 75 deg C or more (cooked tangzhong, Kochstück, empois)
k_by_method.reasoning: fully gelatinized starch let a dough carry 1.1 g more water per g (equal rheology); flour is about 70 % starch, so about 0.75 point per % of flour scalded

accounting.formula: F_s = s * F; W_s = r * F_s; W_total = H * F / 100; W_dough = W_total - W_s - other stages; require W_dough >= 0, i.e. s <= H / (100 * r)
accounting.evaporation: weigh flour + water before cooking (W1) and the paste after cooling (W2); add W1 - W2 back to the dough water
accounting.reasoning: mass balance: every gram of scald flour and water is counted once in the recipe totals

recommended_share_pct.note: water limit: at most about 14 % of flour at 70 % hydration
tested range measured; above 30 % creators report lower volume (science-flour-0092 disagreement on staling)

values.dough_stiffness: G', G'' and yield stress rise at equal water

dough_and_fermentation.note: scalded flour does not feed a fresh levain build; a fermented rye scald reaches pH 3.6 and TTA 12.5 on its own (science-flour-0087)

values.rye_scald_maltose_g_100g: 11.8 (no malt) to 18.2 (1.5 % malt); 25-28 per 100 g dry matter in a bakery scald

softness_staling.hardening_model: H(t) = H_L - (H_L - H_0) * exp(-A * (theta_m - theta)^3 * t); control theta_m 67.6 deg C, A 7.20e-8; yudane 20 % theta_m 58.8 deg C, A 1.22e-7 (per h per deg C^3)

worked_example.yudane: 1000 g flour (T65, H_base 66 %), yudane 20 % at 1:1: dH = 0.15 * 20 = 3.0, H = 69 %, total water 690 g; scald 200 g flour + 200 g boiling water; 490 g water left for the dough
worked_example.tangzhong: 1000 g flour (H_base 66 %), tangzhong 6.25 % at 1:5 cooked to 80 deg C: dH = 0.75 * 6.25 = 4.69, H = 70.7 %, total water 706.9 g; scald 62.5 g flour + 312.5 g water; 394.4 g left
worked_example.share_limit: at H = 70 % a 1:5 tangzhong can take at most 70 / (100 * 5) = 14 % of the flour; 1:2 at most 35 %
worked_example.sugar_check: enriched dough with 20 % sugar and 60 % water: c = 20 / 80 = 25 %, sucrose onset = 65.80 + (72.23 - 65.80) * 10 / 15 = 70.1 deg C, complete near 82 deg C; a scald made from that dough's liquid needs heating well above 65 deg C

vital_gluten.use: Raise a flour's protein to a target with vital wheat gluten, and add the water the gluten takes.

composition.note: use the label value; the Codex standard (CXS 163) could not be retrieved, so its minimum protein is not stated here

additive.conditions: P_f < P_t < P_g, all on the same basis and nitrogen factor; G = 0 when P_t <= P_f

replacement.formula: x = F * (P_t - P_f) / (P_g - P_f) g of the flour replaced by gluten, total flour-equivalent unchanged
replacement.reasoning: same mass balance with fixed total

dry_basis.formula: G = F * (1 - m_f) * (P_t,dm - P_f,dm) / ((1 - m_g) * (P_g,dm - P_t,dm)), P_dm = P_as_is / (1 - m)
dry_basis.note: differs from the as-is result by under 2 % for usual moistures

basis_conversions.moisture: P_dm = P_as_is / (1 - m); US commercial specs at 14 % moisture: P_14 = P_as_is * 86 / (100 - m_percent)

water.rule: +1.5 points of dough water per 1 % gluten added

typical_dose_pct.example: a French reference rye bread (66 % rye) adds 1 % gluten

protein_targets_pct.bread: soft Asian pan loaf, enriched rolls

protein_targets_pct.note: gluten is only 60-80 % of wholemeal protein

worked_example.replacement: same target with total flour fixed at 1000 g: x = 1000 * 2.0 / 64.0 = 31.25 g gluten replacing 31.25 g flour; check (968.75 * 11 + 31.25 * 75) / 1000 = 13.00 %
worked_example.dry_basis: flour at 14 % and gluten at 8.2 % moisture: G = 32.64 g (1.2 % more than the as-is result)
